description: A Community Effort Stems Runoff to Safeguard Corals in Puerto Rico is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Puerto Rico Department of Natural and Environmental Resources; NOAA Office for Coastal Management; NOAA Coral Reef Conservation Program. In Culebra, Puerto Rico, the community used green infrastructure to decrease coastal erosion and mitigate damage to their near-shore coral reef. Coverage: the United States (2021). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Project managers used an open-source digital tool called OpenNSPECT , from NOAA's Office for Coastal Management, to determine the impact of their work. Using baseline water quality data, managers can evaluate the success of the restoration project. Initial reviews of the data indicate overall sediment levels in Tamarindo’s marine habitats have decreased.
